about.description: Live meeting transcription, with Catalan at its heart. Everything is processed on this computer: audio and text never leave it. Local means private.

app.missingModelBody: Murmur transcribes with a model that runs on this computer. You only need to download it once.
app.emptyBody: Record a meeting and the transcript will appear live, split by speaker. Everything is processed on this computer: local means private.

alerts.text: Murmur stays in the system tray: one click and it starts recording.

models.introChoose: Murmur works with models that run on this computer. You only need to download them once.
models.transcriptionText: Turns speech into text, in Catalan and other languages, right on this computer.
models.localText: Gemma 4, by Google, runs on this computer. It takes {{size}} and needs 16 GB of memory.

permissions.micDeniedHelp: Allow microphone access in the system's privacy settings.

permissions.micDenied: Denied. Allow microphone access in the system's privacy settings.
permissions.micUndetermined: If the system asks, allow access.

intelligence.privacyCloud: Each time a summary is generated, the transcript's text and the notes are sent to {{provider}}. The audio never leaves this computer, and the key is saved in the system keychain.

share.privacy: Only what you choose when sharing is sent, encrypted on this computer. The audio only if you tick it.

claude.intro: With the connector, Claude can read and search your meetings and transcribe audio on this computer with Murmur. Transcription happens here, and Claude only gets the text it asks for.
claude.desktopMissing: Claude Desktop isn't on this computer. You can also use it with Claude Code.
claude.privacy: Murmur sends nothing on its own: Claude only gets the text it asks the tools for, and handles it under your terms with Anthropic. Audio never leaves the computer.

share.privacy: Murmur encrypts it on this computer before sending it to your Cloudflare Worker. Without the link nobody can read it, not even Cloudflare.
share.privacyPassword: Murmur encrypts it on this computer before sending it to your Cloudflare Worker. Without the link and the password nobody can read it, not even Cloudflare.
